title: Hyperdescent as orthogonality to local quasi-isomorphisms
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small category with a Grothendieck topology specified by covering sieves: a sieve is a set of arrows with fixed target closed under precomposition, the maximal sieve covers, and covering sieves are stable under pullback and satisfy transitivity. No fibre products in $\mathcal C$ or subcanonicity are assumed. Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring. Let $\mathcal P=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}},\operatorname{Mod}_\Lambda)$ be the abelian category of presheaves of $\Lambda$-modules, with kernels and cokernels computed objectwise. Use cochain complexes and quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $\mathbf D(\mathcal P)$ denote their enhanced localization at objectwise quasi-isomorphisms, retaining derived mapping complexes $R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal P}(-,-)$ and coherent composition [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. For a morphism $f:P\to Q$ of complexes in $\mathcal P$, call $f$ a local quasi-isomorphism if $\bigl(T\mapsto H^i(f(T))\bigr)^\#$ is an isomorphism for every $i\in\mathbf Z$, where $\#$ is sheafification of module presheaves [def-weil-pbc-sheafification].

A hypercover $U_\bullet\to h_T$ is an augmented simplicial presheaf of sets whose terms are coproducts of representables $h_S(V)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(V,S)$ and whose maps to the augmented matching presheaves become epimorphisms after sheafification. The matching presheaf in degree $n$ parametrizes all compatible proper faces of an $n$-simplex, with degree zero matching presheaf $h_T$. If $U_n=\coprod_{\alpha}h_{S_{n,\alpha}}$, put $G(U_n)=\prod_{\alpha}G(S_{n,\alpha})$.

For every complex $G$ in $\mathcal P$, the following are equivalent:
(1) for every hypercover $U_\bullet\to h_T$, the map $G(T)\to\operatorname{holim}_{[n]\in\Delta}G(U_n)$ is an equivalence in the enhanced derived category of $\Lambda$-modules;
(2) for every local quasi-isomorphism $f:P\to Q$, the map
$$R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal P}(Q,G)\longrightarrow R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal P}(P,G)$$
is a quasi-isomorphism of derived mapping complexes.
Here $\Delta$ is the category of nonempty finite ordered sets and weakly increasing maps, and $\operatorname{holim}$ has the coherent limiting-cone meaning of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. No boundedness hypothesis is imposed on $P,Q,G$.

source.place: Choudhury--Gallauer Alves de Souza, Homotopy theory of dg sheaves, arXiv:1511.02828v1, Definition 5.1, Definitions 5.6 and 5.9, Theorem 5.7 and Lemma 5.10, printed pp. 17--20; Lemma 3.19, printed p. 13, identifies descent totalization with the homotopy limit. Homological indices are converted by K_n = K^{-n}. The orthogonality formulation is the defining universal property of the left Bousfield localization in Theorem 5.7, tested on every shift; it concerns the objectwise presheaf derived category, not the sought equivalence with derived sheaves. PDF read in this sandbox; archive in project literature WANTED (the shared repository is read-only).

proof.text: For $T\in\mathcal C$ set $L_T(V)=\Lambda[\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(V,T)]$. For $U_\bullet\to h_T$ form the complex $A_U^{-n}=\bigoplus_\alpha L_{S_{n,\alpha}}$ for $n\ge0$, zero in positive degrees, with alternating-face differential, and augmentation $e_U:A_U\to L_T[0]$. For $i<j$, the identity $d_i d_j=d_{j-1}d_i$ pairs the terms in the square of the differential with opposite signs; in degree one, the two composites to $h_T$ agree, so the augmentation kills $d_0-d_1$. For any presheaf $M$, a module-presheaf map $L_T\to M$ is uniquely determined by the image of the generator $\mathrm{id}_T$, and that element $x\in M(T)$ gives the map taking the generator $a:V\to T$ to $M(a)x$. Thus $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal P}(L_T,M)=M(T)$; maps from a coproduct give the product of these evaluations.

source.place: Definitions 5.1 and 5.3, printed pp. 17-18; free-representable evaluation and alternating-face construction written out Online source read; archived copy WANTED in report.md.

proof.text: Apply [lem-cbc-presheaf-dg-function-complex] to $L_T[0]$ and $A_U$: both are bounded above and termwise coproducts of free representables, whereas $G$ need not be bounded. It gives $R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal P}(L_T[0],G)\simeq G(T)$ and computes $R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal P}(A_U,G)$ by the ordinary Hom complex. Its degree $r$ is $\prod_{n\ge0}G(U_n)^{r-n}$. Regrade the component $h_n$ in degree $r$ by $h_n\mapsto(-1)^{rn+n(n-1)/2}h_n$. In the Hom differential $d_Gh_n-(-1)^r h_{n-1}d_A$, this changes the internal coefficient to $(-1)^n$ and the coface coefficient to $1$. Hence it identifies the complex with $\operatorname{Tot}_{\Pi}(n\mapsto G(U_n))$ having differential $\delta+(-1)^n d_G$. By [lem-cbc-cosimplicial-complex-holim] this is the coherent homotopy limit. The map induced by $e_U$ has only its $n=0$ component, namely restriction from $T$; the augmentation clause of that same node identifies it with the given descent map. Therefore condition (1) is equivalent to $R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal P}(e_U,G)$ being a quasi-isomorphism for every hypercover.

source.place: Definition 5.3 and Remark 5.4, printed p. 18, with Lemma 3.19, printed p. 13; explicit cochain sign and augmentation comparison Online source read; archived copy WANTED in report.md.

proof.text: For any complex map $a:X\to Y$, [lem-cbc-presheaf-dg-function-complex] identifies the map of homotopy groups of $\operatorname{Map}(a[k],G)$ in degree $m\ge0$ with the map on $H^{-m-k}R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal P}(a,G)$. These are maps of simplicial abelian group models, so translation treats every basepoint. If the derived Hom map is a quasi-isomorphism, all these mapping-space maps are equivalences. Conversely, equivalence for every $k$ implies, already at $m=0$, an isomorphism on $H^{-k}$ for every integer $k$, hence a quasi-isomorphism by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. In particular Step 2 identifies (1) with space-locality for all shifted augmentations $e_U[k]$.

source.place: Proof of Lemma 5.10, printed p. 19; cochain reindexing and all integer shifts Online source read; archived copy WANTED in report.md.

proof.text: Choose the small set $\mathcal H_0$ and its set $S$ of shifted augmentation maps from [lem-cbc-hypercover-localization-generation]. That node states that $\mathbf D(\mathcal P)$ is presentable, so [lem-coef-infinity-small-localization-saturation] applies to this genuinely small $S$ in the chosen universes. It says precisely that every arrow in $\langle S\rangle$ induces an equivalence of mapping spaces into each $S$-local object. The generation node identifies the image of every local quasi-isomorphism of complexes with an arrow in this class. This invocation uses the generic small-localization theorem in the objectwise presheaf derived category, without identifying that category with derived sheaves.

source.place: Fact 5.2 and Theorem 5.11, printed pp. 17 and 19-21; strong-saturation restatement via the cited generic localization theorem Online source read; archived copy WANTED in report.md.

proof.text: Assume (1). Steps 2-3 show that $G$ is $S$-local. Let $f:P\to Q$ be any local quasi-isomorphism. For every $k\in\mathbf Z$, the shifted map $f[k]$ is still a local quasi-isomorphism, since its $r$-th cohomology presheaf map is the $(r+k)$-th cohomology presheaf map of $f$. Step 4 and [lem-coef-infinity-small-localization-saturation] therefore give equivalences $\operatorname{Map}(Q[k],G)\to\operatorname{Map}(P[k],G)$ for all $k$. The comparison of [lem-cbc-presheaf-dg-function-complex] on $\pi_0$ gives isomorphisms on $H^{-k}R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal P}(f,G)$ for every integer $k$. These are all cohomology groups, so this derived Hom map is a quasi-isomorphism. This proves (2) for arbitrary unbounded $P,Q$.

source.place: Theorem 5.11 and Definition 5.9, printed pp. 19-21; argument on all shifts, using the defining local-object property expanded in Step 4 Online source read; archived copy WANTED in report.md.

proof.text: Assume (2). For every hypercover $U_\bullet\to h_T$, [lem-cbc-hypercover-localization-generation] says that $e_U:A_U\to L_T[0]$ itself is a local quasi-isomorphism, including hypercovers outside the chosen small family. Apply (2) to this actual map of complexes. The resulting quasi-isomorphism of derived Hom complexes is identified in Step 2, using [lem-cbc-presheaf-dg-function-complex] and [lem-cbc-cosimplicial-complex-holim], with the map $G(T)\to\operatorname{holim}_nG(U_n)$ and its specified augmentation cone. Thus (1) holds for every hypercover. All matching objects used above were presheaf matching objects, so this argument used neither fibre products in $\mathcal C$ nor subcanonicity, and none of the three cited foundations imposes a bound on $G$.

Item statement unchanged and true: objects local for local quasi-isos are the hypercomplete sheaves, which are the objects with hyperdescent; no boundedness needed. Step 2: I recomputed the sign regrading eps=(-1)^{rn+n(n-1)/2}. It gives D=delta+(-1)^n d_G, and eps(r,0)=1 so the augmentation is restriction. Step 3: H^0 RHom(X[k],G)=H^{-k}, so all shifts cover all degrees. Steps 4-6: the generation node supplies a small set S and the HTT tool's closure conventions match. The new nodes are true by K-projectivity of bounded-above complexes of projectives with Dold-Kan of tau<=0, the filtered/Milnor proof that Tot_Pi computes holim over Delta, and the Bousfield localization at hypercovers in the style of Dugger-Hollander-Isaksen. I tested them on the empty site, the topology where the empty sieve covers, the trivial topology, Lambda=0 and a constant cosimplicial diagram. They are not duplicates of K-projective, mapping-comparison, Roos-limit, coproduct-total or hypercover-free-module nodes; none restates a parent clause and there is no cycle. lean.statement: theorem hyperdescent_local_orthogonality {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] (J : GrothendieckTopology C) {Λ : Type w} [CommRing Λ] (G : CochainComplex (Cᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleCat.{max u v w t} Λ) ℤ) : (∀ U : AugmentedFamily.{u, v, max w t} C, IsHypercover J U → HomQuasiIso (augmentationMap.{u, v, w, t} Λ U) G) ↔ (∀ (P Q : CochainComplex (Cᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleCat.{max u v w t} Λ) ℤ) (f : P ⟶ Q), IsLocalQuasiIso.{u, v, w, t} J f → DerivedHomQuasiIso (A := Cᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleCat.{max u v w t} Λ) f G)
lean.note: Second reading replaced unconstrained predicates with semirepresentable augmented simplicial presheaves, local matching lifts, and the canonical free alternating-face augmentation. Both quasi-isomorphism conclusions are tested in every degree via Mathlib Hom-complex/homotopy-category and derived-localization Hom identifications. The underlying-set sheafification test detects exactly isomorphisms of sheafified module maps.
